reason: The crank and ratchet wheel appear to belong with the winding drum, which will wind the lifting cord.
expectation: They will form a hand-operated winding mechanism.

effect: The drum and crank form a hand winch; the longer crank provides more turning effect at the cost of greater hand travel.
reaction: The trade-off between turning effect and hand travel is interesting.
reason: The winch needs to be mounted on the crane before it can lift a load.
expectation: The winch will attach to the crane frame.

effect: The hand winch is now mounted on the crane, ready for the lifting cord.
reaction: The assembly is progressing as expected.
reason: The cord and hook should connect the winch to a load through the tip pulley.
expectation: The cord will be routed over the pulley and attached to the winch.

effect: The crane now has a lifting line, but it still needs a way to hold a load.
reason: The pawl and release lever should let the ratchet hold the winch and release it for lowering.
expectation: The pawl will attach to the winch's ratchet to hold the lifting line.

effect: The pawl can hold the rope, but the crane still needs stability against tipping.
reaction: The distinction between holding the load and keeping the crane upright is useful.
reason: The rear ballast should help counter the load before testing the crane.
expectation: The ballast will attach to the rear of the crane to help resist tipping.

alternatives.reason: I could test it first, but the warning makes adding ballast seem prudent.

effect: The ballast could not be combined yet, so I need to try another step before adding it.
reaction: That was unexpected after the warning about tipping.
reason: The padded test weight looks like the intended safe load for checking the rigged crane.
expectation: The crane will lift and hold the test weight, revealing whether it is stable.

effect: The test showed that the pawl holds the rope, but the crane begins to tip; ballast now has a clear purpose.
reaction: The distinction between holding and balancing the load is clearer after the test.
reason: The rear ballast should counter the test load and keep the rear feet down.
expectation: The ballast will attach to the rear and improve the crane's balance.

effect: The ballast keeps the feet down during the supported test, and the pawl can hold the load while the release lever allows controlled lowering.
reaction: Seeing balance and holding tested separately made their different jobs clear.
reason: The crane has passed its low test, so the cargo basket is the natural next load.
expectation: The crane will lift, hold and gently lower the basket.

effect: The basket test confirmed that the crane can lift, hold and gently lower its cargo, completing the goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate holding and balance fixes work together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the crane and then adding ballast made the difference between holding a load and preventing a tip concrete and worth learning.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the ballast before the test was frustrating: the warning suggested a need for it, but it could not be fitted yet.

surprise.text: The pawl held the rope even as the crane began to tip; those were two different problems.

arbitrary.text: Requiring the tipping test before allowing the ballast felt somewhat arbitrary, since its purpose was already clear from the warning.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the hands-on tests and explanations of how the mechanisms work were interesting, despite the constrained ballast sequence.
